content_zh:
第四百零一章苍白大帝
感受到力量再次涌上来的林奇没有犹豫，转身朝着楼上走去。
先跟菲尔德合力处理掉基拉，之后找时间通过纽扣联系一下玛门...
大家已经认识这么久了，是时候做第一份【交易】了。
......
长刃在空中划过一道弧线，刀锋指向基拉的手腕。
这一刀快得几乎没有影子，连油灯的火苗都没有被刀风带偏。
酒杯在刀锋触及手腕之前被基拉随手抛起。
暗红色的液体从酒杯中泼洒出来，在空中拉出一道弧形的液桥。
基拉后退一步的动作看起来并不快，甚至带着某种老人般的迟缓，但菲尔德那一刀却刚好从他指尖前方两寸的位置划过，连皮肤都没有碰到。
液桥在两人之间断裂，泼洒在地上的液体没有渗入木板的缝隙，像活物一样在地板上蠕动着汇聚成一滩，然后迅速蒸发成淡红色的雾气。
雾气升腾起来的瞬间，整个书房的气温骤降。
“这里作为你的墓地似乎也不错。”基拉站在那团淡红色的雾气中间，声音低沉。
菲尔德没有回应。
他横握长刃，刀锋朝外，脚下踩着碎步在雾气中缓慢移动。
那些蠕动的雾气每一次接触到菲尔德的皮肤，都会带来一阵细微的刺痛。
“死亡是归处。”基拉的声音从雾气中的某个方向传来，方位飘忽不定，像是说话的人在不断移动，又像是雾气本身在替他发声。
雾气忽然向两侧分开。
基拉从雾中走出来，他的头发和双眼变为了苍白色，宛如凝固的月光一样。
他手中多了一把武器。

那是一把双手巨镰，比基拉本人还高出半个头。
镰刃弯如新月，刃面上流转着和基拉眼睛同样的苍白光芒。
镰柄是某种深黑色的木材，表面刻满了密密麻麻的倒三角眼睛符号，那些符号在基拉握上去的瞬间全部睁开了。
每一个倒三角中间的眼睛都变成了一颗真实的、会眨动的、布满血丝的眼球，上下左右地转动着，扫视着书房的每一个角落。
最后所有眼球同时停下，全部聚焦在菲尔德身上。
“你觉得今天谁会死？”基拉将巨镰横在身前，苍白的瞳孔注视着菲尔德。
菲尔德没有等他说完。
在基拉说出最后一个字的瞬间，刀刃已经刺到了基拉胸前的位置。
这一刀没有任何起手式，没有任何预兆，菲尔德的身体从静止到极速的切换几乎违反了物理法则。
刀尖在即将刺入基拉胸膛的时候被巨镰的镰柄挡住了。
金属碰撞的声音在书房中炸开，冲击波将书桌上的纸张全部掀飞到空中。
那些散页的羊皮纸在蓝绿色的灯光下像一群受惊的白色飞蛾，扑棱着翅膀朝四面散去。
基拉单手持镰，另一只手从镰柄上掰下一颗眼球。
那颗眼球在他掌心里转动了一下，瞳孔对准了菲尔德，然后炸开。
没有血肉，没有液体，眼球炸开的瞬间化作一团苍白的火焰，火焰中心温度并不高，但散发出的寒气让菲尔德握着刀把的手指表面结了一层薄霜。
苍白之火顺着刀身蔓延上来，火焰舔过的地方，金属表面开始出现细密的裂纹。
菲尔德松开长刀，让其从右手落到左手，在换手的间隙他踢出一脚，目标是基拉的膝盖。

Chapter 401 The Pale Emperor
Lin Qi, who felt the power surge up again, turned around and walked upstairs without hesitation.
Let's work together with Field to deal with Kira first, and then find time to contact Mammon through the button...
We’ve known each other for so long, it’s time to make our first [deal].
...
The long blade drew an arc in the air, and the blade pointed at Kira's wrist.
The knife was so fast that there was almost no shadow, and even the flame of the oil lamp was not deflected by the wind of the knife.
The wine glass was thrown up by Kira before the blade touched her wrist.
Dark red liquid splashed out from the wine glass, drawing an arc-shaped liquid bridge in the air.
Kira's step back didn't look very fast, even with a kind of slowness like an old man, but Field's knife just passed two inches in front of his fingertips, without even touching the skin.
The liquid bridge broke between the two of them, and the liquid spilled on the ground did not penetrate into the gaps in the wooden boards. It squirmed on the floor like a living thing and gathered into a pool, and then quickly evaporated into a light red mist.
The moment the fog rose, the temperature in the entire study dropped sharply.
"This seems to be a good place for your cemetery." Kira stood in the middle of the light red mist with a low voice.
Field did not respond.
He held the long blade horizontally, with the blade pointing outwards, and moved slowly in the mist with broken steps.
Every time the wriggling mist touches Field's skin, it will bring a slight sting.
"Death is the place to go." Kira's voice came from a certain direction in the fog. The direction was erratic, as if the speaker was constantly moving, or as if the fog itself was speaking for him.
The mist suddenly parted to both sides.
Kira walked out of the fog, his hair and eyes turning pale, like frozen moonlight.
He has an extra weapon in his hand.
It was a two-handed giant scythe, half a head taller than Kira himself.
The sickle blade is curved like a crescent moon, and the same pale light as Kira's eyes flows on the blade surface.
The handle of the sickle was made of some kind of dark black wood, and its surface was engraved with densely packed inverted triangle eye symbols. Those symbols all opened the moment Kira held it.
The eye in the middle of each inverted triangle has turned into a real, blinking, bloodshot eyeball, rotating up and down, left and right, scanning every corner of the study.
Finally, all the eyeballs stopped at the same time, focusing on Field.
"Who do you think will die today?" Kira held the giant scythe in front of her and stared at Field with her pale pupils.
Field didn't wait for him to finish.
The moment Kira said the last word, the blade had already pierced Kira's chest.
There was no starting point for this knife, no warning, and Field's body's switch from stillness to extreme speed almost violated the laws of physics.
The tip of the knife was blocked by the handle of the giant scythe when it was about to pierce Kira's chest.
The sound of metal colliding exploded in the study room, and the shock wave lifted all the papers on the desk into the air.
Those loose pages of parchment looked like a flock of frightened white moths under the blue-green light, flapping their wings and scattering in all directions.
Kira held the sickle in one hand and pried off an eyeball from the handle with the other hand.
The eyeball turned in his palm, the pupils were aimed at Field, and then exploded.
There was no flesh and blood, and no liquid. The moment the eyeball exploded, it turned into a ball of pale flame. The temperature in the center of the flame was not high, but the cold air emitted made Field's fingers holding the handle of the knife form a thin layer of frost.
The pale fire spread along the blade, and where the flames licked, fine cracks began to appear on the metal surface.
Field let go of the long knife and let it fall from his right hand to his left hand. During the change of hands, he kicked out, aiming at Kira's knee.
